title: Buckwheat Blueberry Waffles
changes_from_base: All buckwheat flour (no wheat), dark brown sugar, nutmeg and buttermilk, with whites whisked to medium peaks and blueberries and lemon zest folded in.
summary: Nutty buckwheat waffles studded with blueberries and bright lemon zest, finished with warm maple syrup.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
large eggs, at room temperature, separated
unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the iron

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk 174 g buckwheat flour, 42 g dark brown sugar, 1 tsp baking powder, ½ tsp nutmeg, ¼ tsp bicarbonate of soda and ⅛ tsp salt together and make a well in the centre.

steps.title: Separate
steps.text: Put 2 egg whites in one bowl, then drop the 2 egg yolks into the well along with 240 ml buttermilk and stir gently into a batter without overmixing.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the egg whites to medium peaks, add to the batter and fold in gently until just combined.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Fold in 30 g melted butter, then 140 g blueberries and 1½ tbsp grated lemon zest.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the waffle iron and brush lightly with butter.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pour about 160 ml batter per waffle and cook until golden and crisp, buttering the iron between batches.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve as they're ready, or keep warm in a 93 °C oven, with warm maple syrup.

tips: Fold the whisked egg whites in gently, scooping from the bottom of the bowl, to keep the batter light.
Use frozen blueberries straight from the freezer rather than thawing them, so they don't bleed colour through the batter.
Brush the iron lightly with butter between batches as needed so each waffle releases cleanly.
storage: Best eaten fresh and warm, straight from the iron. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
